{{Expand Japanese}}

{{Infobox Japanese clan|founder={{ill|Amanomichine|ja|天道根命|en|Amanomichine}} (mythical)<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />
Ōnagusahiko (historical) <ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />|image=File:Hinokuma Shrine.JPG|caption=Hinokuma Shrine, the traditional shrine of the family|parent house=[[Kuni no miyatsuko]]|image caption=Hinokuma Shrine, the traditional shrine of the family|alt=Hinokuma Shrine, the traditional shrine of the family|province of origin={{ill|Kii Province|en|Kii Province|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}|home province={{ill|Kii Province|en|Kii Province|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}}}

{{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀伊国造|fr|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko}} is a [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no miyatsuko]] that had a uniquely high amount of power similar to the {{ill|Izumo clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Izumo clan|Izumo clan}}.<ref name="mw-2023a">{{Cite web |date=2023-03-10 |title=Kuni no miyatsuko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8839 |access-date=2023-12-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230310081317/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8839 |archive-date=2023-03-10 }}</ref>

The Kinoatai family was responsible for this office. According to the Sendai Kuji Hongi, a historic record, Amenomichine no Mikoto, a descendant of Kami Musubi no Mikoto, was the first to be appointed as Ki no Kuni no Miyatsuko during the reign of Emperor Jinmu. However, Ōnagusahiko is often considered the actual precursor of the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀伊国造}}.<ref name="mw-2023a" />

They run [[Hinokuma Shrine|Hinokuma Shrine]].<ref name="mw-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-16|title=Kinokuninomiyatsuko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231216060822/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8597|access-date=2023-12-16|website=web.archive.org}}</ref> and are the Kuni no miyatsuko of {{ill|Kii Province|en|Kii Province|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}.

They descend from {{ill|Amanomichine|ja|天道根命|en|Amanomichine}}<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />.

They are believed to be buried at {{ill|Iwase-Senzuka Kofun Cluster|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Iwase-Senzuka Kofun Cluster|Iwase-Senzuka Kofun Cluster}}<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book|title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia|last1=Isomura|first1=Yukio|last2=Sakai|first2=Hideya|date=2012|publisher=学生社|isbn=43pp750404}}
{{in lang|ja}}</ref>..

They worshipped the daughters of Susanoo.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9161|access-date=2024-04-01|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref>
==Overview==
The Kinoatai family held a title called "Kuni no Miyatsuko" of the {{ill|Kii Province|en|Kii Province|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}. The title meant they were a provincial governor with both religious and secular duties. The title is mentioned in historic texts such as the [[Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]]. The Chinese characters used to write the term in the [[Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] were adopted under the [[Ritsuryō system|Ritsuryō system]], a legal system in ancient Japan, and they can also be read as Kokuzo.<ref name="mw-2023a" />

The system of kuni no miyatsuko includes the chieftain of the Nagusa district, Nagusahiko, who was integrated into the imperial control structure in the early phases of [[kofun]] construction in the fifth century. Some theories suggest the kuni no miyatsuko system was established in the {{ill|6th century|af|6de eeu|als|6. Following the {{ill|Taika Reform|en|Taika Reform}}, which aimed to consolidate imperial power and regulate land ownership in {{ill|645|en|645|qid=Q31040|lt=645}}, the kuni no miyatsuko also served as gunji, or district administrators. This dual role became less common after the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}}.<ref name="mw-2023a" />

The {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀伊国造|fr|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko}} ran the [[Hinokuma Shrine|Hinokuma and Kunikakasu shrines]] and their current descendants serve as gūji, or chief priests. The Jōgan Gishiki, a document from the period, outlines the ritual for appointing the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀伊国造}} who served these shrines.<ref name="mw-2023a" />

This clan of Miyatsuko descended from the {{ill|Shinbetsu|ja|神別}}, specifically the '''Ki-shi''' (紀氏). Historically, they held the dual responsibilities of the office of Miyatsuko in Kii Province and the priestly duties of {{ill|Hinokuma Shrine|en|Hinokuma Shrine|qid=Q888184|lt=Hinokuma Shrine and Kunikakasu Shrine}}. Even after the abolition of the Miyatsuko system during the establishment of the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|qid=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}}, they retained the title "Miyatsuko" as hereditary priests (宮司) of these shrines.

== Overview ==

=== Name Variants ===
In the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}, the name is recorded as 紀伊国造 (Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko). Older texts use variants such as '''Ki no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (木国造) in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and '''Ki no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (紀国造) in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}.

=== Ancestry ===
* The {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}'s "Miyatsuko Chronicle" attributes the establishment of Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko to {{ill|Amanomichine|ja|天道根命}}, a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Kamimusubi|ja|神皇産霊命}}, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}. The {{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|ja|紀伊続風土記}} concurs, stating that Ame no Michine no Mikoto was granted control of Kii Province after Emperor Jimmu’s unification of the Kinai region.
* The first historically verifiable Miyatsuko is likely {{ill|ki no oshikatsu|ja|紀忍勝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Oshikatsu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 紀押勝|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q58139743}}, mentioned in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} (entries for Emperor Bidatsu's 12th year, 7th and 10th months).<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=古代氏族の系譜を読み解く|date=2022nd year 2月1日|publisher=吉川弘文館|page=134|author=鈴木正信}}</ref>

=== Clan Lineage ===
The Ki clan (紀氏) originally held the {{ill|Kimi (kabane)|ja|君 (姓)|lt=Kimi}} title and later transitioned to {{ill|Atai|ja|直 (姓)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Natori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55526687}} in the {{ill|Koseki system in classical Japan|ja|庚午年籍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Nenki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 古代日本の戸籍制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11410913}}. By 835 CE, they received the {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|qid=Q11455653|lt=Sukune}} title.<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男}}「第1章 天神系氏族　第6節 紀国造氏族　1紀国造紀直、紀宿祢（一）」『古代氏族系譜集成』中巻、古代氏族研究会、879-881頁。</ref>

The Ki clan served as priests of Hinokuma and Kunikakasu shrines for over two millennia. The preservation of such a lineage, aside from the Imperial Family, is rare. Comparable examples include the {{ill|Izumo Miyatsuko|ja|Izumo Province 造}} lineages of the Senge and Kitajima families and priestly clans such as the {{ill|Aso Shrine|en|Aso Shrine|qid=Q715639|lt=Aso Shrine}}'s Aso family or the {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|Sumiyoshi-taisha|qid=Q705949|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}}'s Tsumori family.<ref>『[[Jōgan Gishiki|貞観儀式]]』巻第10。</ref>

== Historical Evolution ==
The Miyatsuko family adapted through Japan’s tumultuous history. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, they maintained regional influence through alliances with the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|qid=Q1069187|lt=Kii Domain}} and others. Despite the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}’s challenges, including the {{ill|Battle of Kishuu|ja|紀州征伐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Siege of Kii Province|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10855721}}, the clan continued to serve as priests and feudal administrators.

=== Transition to Modern Era ===
In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the family entered the {{ill|Kazoku|en|Kazoku|qid=Q241734|lt=Kazoku}} peerage system, obtaining baronial status. Members served in government roles, such as {{ill|Toshihide Kii|ja|紀俊秀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Baron Ki Toshihide|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11604973}}, who represented the family in the {{ill|Chamber of Peers|en|Chamber of Peers|qid=Q2948408|lt=House of Peers}}.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|date=2006th year （平成18th year ）|title=華族 近代日本貴族の虚像と実像|author=小田部雄次|authorlink=小田部雄次|publisher=[[中央公論新社]]|series=[[中公新書]]1836|isbn= 978-4121018366|ref=harv}}</ref>

== Genealogy ==

* The "Ki Clan Genealogy" recorded in {{ill|Sonpi Bunmyaku|en|Sonpi Bunmyaku|qid=Q1704738|lt=Sonpi Bunmyaku}} and {{ill|Gunsho Ruijū|en|Gunsho Ruijū|qid=Q1554852|lt=Gunsho Ruijū}} is inconsistent across generations and cannot be trusted as it stands. Here, , {{ill|Kugyō Bunin|ja|Kugyō補任}}, and {{ill|Ki Clan Genealogical Records|ja|紀氏家牒}}}}, although it is noted that there are still differing opinions regarding the early sections and the positions of individuals such as {{ill|Ki no Maro|ja|紀麻路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki Maji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605129}}, {{ill|Ki no Sarutori|ja|紀猿取|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki Sarutori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q98083047}}, {{ill|Ki no Tanaga|ja|紀田長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki Tanaga|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106196670}}, and {{ill|Ki no Haseo|en|Ki no Haseo|qid=Q118767|lt=Ki Haseo}}.

'''Kinokuno Clan''' (紀氏, ''Ki no Uji'') is a clan whose family name is "Ki."

The Kinokuno Clan was an ancient {{ill|Gōzoku|en|Gōzoku|qid=Q84066|lt=Gōzoku}} based in {{ill|Kinori|ja|紀里}}, Heguri District, Yamato Province (present-day Kamisho, {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|qid=Q1346790|lt=Heguri}}, Ikoma District, Nara Prefecture). Initially holding the title of {{ill|Omi (title)|en|Omi (title)|qid=Q2574718|lt=Omi}}, they were renamed {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|qid=Q4807592|lt=Asomi}} under the {{ill|Yatsuka no Kabane|ja|八色の姓}} system established in the 13th year of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|ja|Emperor Tenmu|2=ja|3=天武天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q335181}}'s reign (684 AD).

== Overview ==

According to sources like the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|記紀}}, the Kinokuno Clan descended from {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ar|الإمبراطور كوغين|arz|الامبراطور كوجين|azb|کوقن (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Kōgen|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆگێن|cs|Kógen|de|Kōgen|es|Kōgen Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوگن|fr|Kōgen (empereur)|hr|Kōgen|hu|Kógen japán császár|id|Kaisar Kōgen|it|Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇|ka|კოგენი|ko|고겐 천황|nl|Kogen|pl|Kōgen|pt|Kogen|ru|Император Когэн|sh|Car Kōgen|simple|Emperor Kōgen|sl|Cesar Kogen|sr|Коген|sv|Kogen (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิโคเง็ง|tl|Emperador Kogen|tr|Kōgen (imparator)|uk|Імператор Коґен|uz|Imperator Kōgen|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōgen|zh|孝元天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôgen Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝元天皇|qid=Q333572|lt=Emperor Kōgen}}, with {{ill|Ki no Tsuno|ja|紀角|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Tsuno|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605107}}, a son of {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|en|Takenouchi no Sukune|qid=Q1073668|lt=Takenouchi no Sukune}}, as their progenitor. Both Ki no Tsuno and his predecessor were maternally descended from the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀氏|de|Ki (Klan)|uk|Рід Кі|ko|기씨 (황별)|fr|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko}} family. This relationship suggests that the clan served the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}} early on as a military house. Figures like {{ill|Ki no Koyumi|ja|紀小弓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Oyu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605024}}, {{ill|Ki no Ōiwa|ja|紀大磐|ko|기노 오이와|qid=Q11605012}}, and {{ill|Ki no Omamaro|ja|紀男麻呂|qid=Q11605087}} were active in military and diplomatic affairs, particularly regarding the Korean Peninsula, during the reigns of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|en|Emperor Yūryaku|qid=Q357235|lt=Emperor Yūryaku}}, {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|en|Emperor Kenzō|qid=Q360966|lt=Emperor Kenzo}}, and {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|qid=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei}}.

Although the Kinokuno Clan belonged to the Takenouchi lineage, like the {{ill|Katsuragi clan|en|Katsuragi clan|qid=Q11620908|lt=Katsuragi Clan}}, {{ill|Kose clan|ja|巨勢氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kose Clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11479778}}, and {{ill|Heguri Clan|ja|平群氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heguri Clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11483498}}, they notably did not produce a {{ill|Minister (government)|en|Minister (government)|qid=Q83307|lt=Ōomi}} before the {{ill|Taika Reform|en|Taika Reform|qid=Q570140|lt=Taika Reform}} period.

During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|en|Emperor Tenji|qid=Q314802|lt=Emperor Tenji}}, {{ill|Ki no Ōtoko|ja|紀大人}} served as the {{ill|yushi dafu|ja|御史大夫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtsukasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11071155}}. In the Nara period, {{ill|Ki no Maro|ja|紀麻呂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Maro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605127}} became a {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|qid=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon}}, {{ill|Ki no Maro|ja|紀麻路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Masaru|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605129}} a {{ill|Chūnagon|en|Chūnagon|qid=Q1185382|lt=Chūnagon}}, and {{ill|Ki no Iimaro|ja|紀飯麻呂|qid=Q11605128}} a {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|qid=Q1133663|lt=Sangi}}. The clan flourished as an {{ill|Consort kin|en|Consort kin|qid=Q1050320|lt=Outer Clan}} after {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|白壁王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Shirakabe|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 光仁天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q958662}}, born to {{ill|Ki no Tochihime|ja|紀橡姫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ki no Tsuji Hime|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24868439}} and {{ill|Prince Shiki|en|Prince Shiki|qid=Q11072254|lt=Prince Shiki}}, ascended as {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|en|Emperor Kōnin|qid=Q958662|lt=Emperor Kōnin}}. However, during the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, the clan's influence waned due to the rise of the {{ill|Fujiwara Hok-ke|en|Fujiwara Hok-ke|qid=Q2975268|lt=Fujiwara Hokke}}.

By the early Heian period, only a few members, such as {{ill|Ki no Haseo|en|Ki no Haseo|qid=Q118767|lt=Ki no Haseo}}, managed to hold significant positions. They later transitioned to literary contributions, producing figures like {{ill|Ki no Tsurayuki|en|Ki no Tsurayuki|qid=Q468288|lt=Ki no Tsurayuki}}, {{ill|Ki no Tomonori|en|Ki no Tomonori|qid=Q1092686|lt=Ki no Tomonori}}, and {{ill|Ki no Tokibumi|en|Ki no Tokibumi|qid=Q3196291|lt=Ki no Tokifumi}}.
